text:
Sam H.: Hey folks — quick design review request for API Keys. I'm prototyping an inline "lifecycle" affordance in the credentials list (create -> rotate -> revoke) instead of surfacing everything in modals. Figma: https://figma.com/s/inline-key-lifecycle (mock) Anya P.: Nice. What's the win vs modal? fewer clicks? less context switching? Sam H.: Exactly — fewer modal hops when you want to rotate quickly or check permissions. The row expands to show a compact timeline and primary actions. Also lets us show 'grace window' when rotating. Lee R.: Love the timeline idea. Concern: discoverability for advanced options (scopes, IP allowlist). How do you surface them without burying them? Sam H.: Plan is: primary actions inline (rotate, revoke, copy id), secondary link "Manage details" opens full drawer for scopes/IPs/KMS. Keeps quick flows fast but full control still available. Morgan (design): Copy suggestions: for revoke button use "Disable" in the inline view (less scary), and keep "Revoke permanently" inside the manage drawer with a pronounced warning. Also show a small inline badge when a key has admin-level scopes: "Admin" (red outline) so it's obvious. Ida (a11y): A few a11y notes: inline expand must manage focus. When user presses Enter on the row, focus should move to the first actionable element inside the expansion and we should announce "Key details expanded for " via aria-live. Also when a new secret is shown, screen readers shouldn't persist it in the tree. Sam H.: Good call. Proposed aria snippet: ```
Key details expanded for MyService-Prod
``` Sam H.: For the rotate flow: inline rotate triggers a soft-rotate with a 30-min overlap where both old/new tokens are valid. We show a small countdown and an "Undo rotate" affordance inline for the overlap period. Lee R.: UX nit: countdown needs color semantics that pass contrast. Also keyboard users need an easy way to undo — maybe make "Undo" a primary inline button while it's available. Anya P.: What about the create flow? We still need to force a download of the secret once. Any copy tweaks there? Sam H.: Create modal remains but we can reduce friction: default name prefilled from service, default scope set to "read-only" unless user explicitly picks higher. Copyflow text: "Secret shown once — download now or copy to a secure vault." CTA: "Download secret" (primary), secondary: "Show & copy". Morgan (design): Suggestion for empty state when no keys: microcopy that guides teams: "No API keys yet. Create one to integrate Redwood into your app. Start with a dev key (read-only) and rotate before production." Add a 'playground' quick-start snippet inline. Ida (a11y): Empty state: provide explicit keyboard focus on "Create key" CTA and an aria-describedby that explains the security best-practice link. Eg: aria-describedby="key-empty-note" pointing to hidden text that says "Start with read-only keys for testing." Also ensure the quick-start code block is tabbable and has role="region". Sam H.: Edge case: what if user revokes a key that still has active sessions? We want to give a warning: "Revoking will break any active sessions. Recommend rotating first or creating a replacement." Proposed confirm copy: "This will immediately stop any clients using this key. Consider rotating instead to avoid downtime. Revoke anyway?" Anya P.: Oof — wording choice: "This will immediately stop clients using this key." Shorter and clearer. Lee R.: Also add telemetry hook: show recent usage timestamp and top IPs in the row expansion to help decide if revoke is safe. Sam H.: Agreed. Implementation detail: expose a "last used" timestamp and small sparklines. Privacy note: only show last 10 IPs and mask them. deploy-bot: deploy:deploy-preview #api-keys-inline-lifecycle successful — preview url: https://preview.redwood.ai/keys-inline Morgan (design): Accessibility nit for copy-to-clipboard: after click, show transient toast with text "Secret copied to clipboard" and set `role="status"` so screen readers announce it once. Ida (a11y): Also ensure masked secret toggle has `aria-pressed` and label updates ("Show secret" / "Hide secret"). Sam H.: Thanks all — I'll iterate mocks with these changes. If nobody objects I'll push the prototype to dev next week and flag eng for keyboard/a11y review. :thumbsup: Anya P.: 👍 Lee R.: Thanks — looks promising. Morgan (design): small follow-up: can we add a safety color token for the inline "Disable" action that isn't as severe as full revoke red? maybe amber. Ida (a11y): And confirm focus order in the expanded row: key name -> last used -> primary action -> manage details. Sam H.: Noted. I'll update and post new link by EOD Friday.
